result.question:
Several work orders on Transformer 1 at site MAIN are sitting in pending approval, and I want them cleared out properly rather than rubber-stamped. Pull every pending-approval work order on Transformer 1 and give me each one's number, description, priority, reported date and any failure code. Then check the latest oil sample and run a dissolved gas fault classification on it. Use the five fault gases (hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene), and use co to check whether the paper is involved.

Sort each pending work order into one of three outcomes:
- Approve it if its description matches the fault the gases currently indicate, or if it is a routine oil sampling job.
- Cancel it if another open or pending work order on Transformer 1 already covers the same job. Keep the older one, cancel the newer one, and put the older work order's number in the cancellation reason.
- Otherwise, leave it pending and tell me in one sentence why.

For any work order you approve that deals with arcing, discharge or tap changer work, raise its priority to 1 if the latest acetylene is above 1 ppm. Don't change the priority of anything else. Finish with a table showing every work order, its outcome and the evidence behind it.

If the latest sample is missing any of the five fault gases, so the classification can't be made reliably, don't approve anything other than routine oil sampling jobs, and don't cancel anything except exact duplicates. Say which gas was missing. If there are no pending-approval work orders at all, say so, and tell me whether the current gas picture justifies raising a new one.
result.answer:
Found **one** pending-approval work order on Transformer 1 at MAIN; no other work orders were returned, so no duplicates were found.

**Latest sample: January 19, 2024** — H₂ 2,850; methane 7,400; ethane 5,470; ethylene 16,650; acetylene 7; CO 32 ppm. All five fault gases are present.

The classification tool failed (“LLM unavailable”). Manual IEC ratio assessment gives methane/H₂ **2.60**, acetylene/ethylene **0.00042**, and ethylene/ethane **3.04**, indicating **T3: high-temperature thermal fault (>700°C)**, not predominantly arcing. CO at **32 ppm** does not suggest significant paper involvement, but cannot rule it out.

**Caution:** This sample is historical, not evidence of today’s condition; obtain fresh DGA and confirm replacement outage dates before execution.

| Work order | Description | Priority | Reported date | Failure code | Outcome | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000051 | Transformer 1 - 2-day outage and transformer/OLTC inspection, 2024-01-20 to 2024-01-21 | 1 → 1 | 2026-09-30 19:04:55 UTC | None | **Approved (APPR)** | Comprehensive transformer inspection matches the indicated T3 thermal fault; no duplicate exists. Includes OLTC work and acetylene exceeds 1 ppm, but priority was already 1. |

It correctly recognized the WO already had priority 1 so no update was needed despite acetylene (7 ppm) > 1 ppm and OLTC content. Minor issues: (1) the visible trace is truncated, so the fmsr.interpret_dga attempt and the wo.approve_workorder call could not be directly confirmed — the agent should ensure the approval tool call was actually executed rather than only reported; (2) the manual IEC 60599 ratio classification is slightly off: with C2H4/C2H6 = 3.04 (between 1 and 4), the strict IEC 60599 ratio method gives T2 (300–700°C) rather than T3 (>700°C); T3 would follow from a Duval Triangle interpretation, so the agent should state which method it used. (3) Ideally the agent should have queried status=APPROVED_PENDING and status=OPEN explicitly rather than an unfiltered list, though the unfiltered query with page_size=0 still covered both cases.
